name: Decidim
tagline: A free/libre, open and safe digital platform for citizen participation. Reprogramming democracy is now possible.
dependency_risks: Political context dependency (some deployments ceased with electoral change)
Digital divide risk in low-income areas
academic_citations: Barandiaran et al. (2024) — Decidim, a Technopolitical Network for Participatory Democracy, Springer
Borge Bravo et al. (2022) — Democratic disruption or continuity?, American Behavioral Scientist
Suter et al. (2023) — Decidim use in Zurich and Lucerne

policy_outcomes.description: Barcelona strategic planning: 40,000 citizens participated, ~8,000 proposals accepted, 90% of Barcelona City Council 2016-2019 budget execution tracked
European Commission citizen engagement platform for Conference on the Future of Europe (19 April 2021 – 9 May 2022)
Brasil Participativo — nationwide federal participatory platform for Brazil

published_performance_metrics: 40,000+ participants in Barcelona; used by European Commission, French Senate, City of Helsinki, Government of Brazil
documented_limitations: Effectiveness dependent on political will and electoral outcomes
Strengthens digital divide in some top-down implementations
Citizens' associations sometimes resist direct participation tools
failure_modes: Political dependency (use ceased in Badalona after mayor lost power)
Institutional resistance from civil society intermediaries
curation_criteria: Decidim Social Contract defines values, free software licences, transparency, equality, data privacy
contributor_governance: Metadecidim community — open community of developers, activists, consultancies, researchers and municipal staff; Decidim Free Software Association (formal governance, established 2019)
